evidence: change-deliverymans-status.dto.ts: ChangeDeliverymansStatusDto { @IsString() @IsNotEmpty() isActive: boolean } is the request shape for deliveryman status; the @IsString on a boolean is a validation bug, not a cohesion issue

update-deliverymans-info.dto.ts: UpdateDeliverymansInfoDto { firstName?, lastName? } with @IsString @IsOptional is the optional version of the create DTO; the overlap is the normal create/update DTO pattern

create-order.dto.ts: CreateOrderDto { name, description } and update-deliverymans-orders.dto.ts: UpdateDeliverymansOrdersDto { description? } cover the deliveryman's orders, used by add-order-to-deliveryman.service.ts and update-deliverymans-orders.service.ts
All files import only from class-validator and are imported by deliveryman.controller.ts plus one matching service each, so they form one request-validation unit
parsedVerdict.reasoning:
This module passes. All five files do one job: they are class-validator request DTOs for the deliveryman feature. Each DTO is used by deliveryman.controller.ts and by the one service that matches it. The order DTOs (CreateOrderDto, UpdateDeliverymansOrdersDto) are for adding and updating a deliveryman's orders, which is still part of the deliveryman feature, not a separate concern. Every file is built the same way: a plain class with class-validator decorators, and nothing goes around that pattern.

The firstName/lastName fields are written twice, once in CreateDeliverymanDto (@IsNotEmpty) and once in UpdateDeliverymansInfoDto (@IsOptional). That is the usual create/update DTO pair. Deriving one from the other (for example with PartialType) would be tidier, but this does not split an invariant across places in a way that breaks cohesion.

One thing outside this rule is still worth fixing: ChangeDeliverymansStatusDto puts @IsString on a boolean field, isActive. That is a bug that will reject valid boolean values. It is a correctness problem, not a cohesion or boundary problem.
